blogPosts.title: Pool Barrier Compliance in Selby: What Every Homeowner Needs to Know in 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Understanding Victorian pool barrier laws is essential for every Selby homeowner. Learn what your pool fence needs to meet 2026 compliance standards.
body: Living in Selby means enjoying the lush green surroundings of the Dandenong Ranges, and for many local families, that includes a backyard pool or spa. However, Victorian law requires all pool and spa owners to maintain compliant safety barriers at all times. In 2026, the regulations have been updated to further strengthen child safety around water. If you own a pool or spa in Selby, understanding these requirements is not just a legal obligation but a critical step in protecting your loved ones. Non-compliance can result in fines and, more importantly, put children at serious risk.

Under the Victorian Building Act, every pool and spa must have a barrier that meets specific standards. Fences must be at least 1.2 metres high, gates must be self-closing and self-latching, and there must be no gaps greater than 100 millimetres at the base. The latch must be positioned at least 1.5 metres from the ground or on the outside of the gate so young children cannot reach it. For Selby homeowners, these rules apply whether you have an in-ground pool, above-ground pool, or a portable spa. Understanding the specifics ensures you avoid costly non-compliance penalties.

One of the most common compliance issues we see during inspections in Selby involves gate latches that have worn out over time. The Dandenong Ranges experience significant moisture and temperature fluctuations, which can cause metal components to corrode or plastic parts to degrade. Self-closing hinges may lose their tension, meaning gates no longer swing shut automatically. Vegetation growth near pool fences is another frequent problem in Selby, where the leafy environment means plants can quickly obscure barrier lines and create climbing opportunities for children.

During a Swim Safe pool barrier inspection in Selby, we conduct a thorough assessment of every element of your pool or spa barrier system. This includes measuring fence heights, checking gate operation, testing self-closing and self-latching mechanisms, inspecting for climbable objects near the barrier, and verifying that no gaps exceed the maximum allowance. Our inspector will also check that the barrier separates the pool area from the house correctly, which is a common oversight in Selby homes where internal doors provide direct pool access without appropriate hardware.

To prepare for your pool barrier inspection in Selby, walk around your pool area and check for obvious issues. Ensure gates close and latch on their own, trim back any vegetation growing near the fence, remove climbable furniture or pots from within one metre of the barrier, and check that the fence panels are secure and undamaged. If you notice any concerns, addressing them before the inspection can save time and help you pass on the first visit. Our team at Swim Safe is always happy to provide pre-inspection guidance over the phone.

Choosing Swim Safe for your Selby pool barrier inspection means working with a team that has over 40 years of building industry experience. We are passionate about pool safety because we are parents too, and we understand the peace of mind that comes from knowing your barrier is fully compliant. Contact us today to book your inspection and ensure your Selby property meets all Victorian pool safety requirements for 2026.

blogPosts.title: Preparing Your Pool Fence for Summer: A Selby Homeowner's Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Summer is peak pool season in Selby. Discover how to prepare your pool fence for compliance before the warm weather arrives.
body: Summer in Selby means long, warm days perfect for swimming, but before you dive in, it is essential to ensure your pool fence is ready for the season. Pool barriers endure significant wear throughout the year, and the cooler, wetter months in the Dandenong Ranges can take a toll on gate mechanisms, fence panels, and latch hardware. A pre-summer inspection of your pool barrier is a smart move for every Selby homeowner, ensuring your family can enjoy the pool safely and in full compliance with Victorian regulations.

The first thing to check as summer approaches is your pool gate. Open it fully and let it swing shut on its own. Does it close completely and latch without assistance? Self-closing hinges can lose tension over time, especially in the Dandenong Ranges where humidity and temperature changes affect metal springs. If your gate does not close on its own, this is a compliance failure. Replacing self-closing hinges is a straightforward fix that Selby homeowners can often handle themselves, or our team at Swim Safe can advise you on the best solution.

Next, examine the latch mechanism on your pool gate. Victorian regulations require latches to be at least 1.5 metres above the ground if accessible from the outside, or positioned so a child under five cannot operate them. Test the latch to ensure it engages firmly every time the gate closes. Check for any rust, corrosion, or loose components. The Dandenong Ranges climate can accelerate wear on metal fittings, so Selby homeowners should pay particular attention to brass and steel latches that may have degraded over winter.

Walk around the perimeter of your pool fence and check for gaps at the bottom. Victorian standards specify that no gap between the fence and the ground should exceed 100 millimetres. Over time, ground movement, erosion, or settling can create larger gaps, particularly on sloped Selby properties. Also check the vertical gaps between fence panels, which must not exceed 100 millimetres. If vegetation has grown around the base of your fence, trim it back to ensure clear visibility and eliminate any potential climbing aids for children near the barrier.

The leafy environment of the Dandenong Ranges means Selby pool owners must be vigilant about vegetation management around their pool fence. Trees, shrubs, and even large pot plants positioned too close to the barrier can provide a climbing opportunity for children, effectively negating the fence's protective purpose. Remove or relocate any climbable objects within one metre of the pool fence. This includes garden furniture, storage bins, and decorative features. Regular garden maintenance around your pool barrier is essential for ongoing compliance throughout the swimming season.

Before summer kicks off, schedule a professional pool barrier inspection with Swim Safe in Selby. Our thorough assessment will identify any compliance issues before they become a problem, giving you confidence that your pool fence is ready for the season. With over 40 years of building industry experience, we know exactly what inspectors look for and how to help you pass with flying colours. Contact Swim Safe today to book your pre-summer inspection and keep your Selby family safe all season long.

blogPosts.title: Top Pool Safety Mistakes Selby Property Owners Make
blogPosts.excerpt: Avoid the most common pool and spa barrier compliance errors that Selby homeowners face. Learn what inspectors look for during assessments.
body: Every year, pool and spa barrier inspections across Selby and the Dandenong Ranges reveal the same recurring compliance issues. As inspectors with over 40 years of building industry experience, the team at Swim Safe has seen it all. Understanding these common mistakes can help Selby homeowners address problems before their inspection, avoiding the stress and cost of a failed compliance check. Here are the top pool safety mistakes we encounter most frequently in Selby properties and how you can avoid them.

The number one mistake we see in Selby is gates that do not self-close and self-latch properly. This is the most common reason for a pool barrier inspection failure in Victoria. Over time, self-closing hinges lose their spring tension, particularly in the damp Dandenong Ranges climate. Gate latches can also become misaligned or corroded. Selby homeowners should test their pool gate regularly by opening it fully and confirming it closes and latches without being pushed. If it does not, the hinges or latch need attention before your inspection.

The second most frequent issue is climbable objects positioned too close to the pool fence. Victorian regulations state that no climbable object should be within one metre of the outside of a pool barrier. In Selby, we regularly find outdoor furniture, garden beds, storage sheds, and even large rocks placed in the climbable zone. Children can use these objects to scale the fence and gain access to the pool area. A quick walk around your pool fence from a child's perspective will help you identify potential climbing aids that need to be relocated.

Many Selby property owners are unaware that their pool barrier must also prevent direct access from the house to the pool area without passing through a compliant gate. Internal doors leading to the pool must be fitted with self-closing and self-latching devices, or the door must remain locked at all times. This is a frequently overlooked requirement in Selby homes, particularly older properties where renovations may have altered the original pool access layout. Ensuring house-to-pool access meets standards is just as important as the external fence itself.

Spa barrier compliance is another area where Selby homeowners often fall short. Many assume that a portable spa or a spa with a cover does not require a compliant barrier, but Victorian law is clear: any spa capable of holding more than 300 millimetres of water must have a compliant barrier if it is not fenced by the pool barrier itself. Lockable spa lids must meet specific standards. Selby residents with spas should ensure they understand the requirements, as non-compliance carries the same penalties as a pool barrier failure.

Regular professional inspections are the best way to stay ahead of pool safety compliance in Selby. At Swim Safe, we recommend annual barrier checks to catch wear and tear before it becomes a compliance issue. With 40 plus years in the building industry and a deep knowledge of Victorian pool safety regulations, we help Selby families maintain safe, compliant pool and spa barriers year-round. Contact us today to schedule your inspection and avoid the common mistakes that catch so many Dandenong Ranges property owners off guard.
